Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

manufacturer noun

also maker, producer, manufacturers, made by, the makers

classical

Cic. Off. 1.150: opificēs omnēs in sordidā arte versantur (Lewis & Short)

opifex, opificis m. f.

a maker, a craftsman who makes things

One who makes a work (opus + facere): a workman or artisan, and in Cicero the maker of the world (N.D. 1.18). Latin usually names the maker with a relative clause: who made this machine?, quis hanc māchinam fēcit?.

Other words

  • officīna, officīnae f. — the works, the firm that makes something

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Suet. Gram. 23: officīnās prōmercālium vestium, workshops making clothes for sale (Lewis & Short); Caes. BC 1.34: officīna armōrum, an arms works (Lewis & Short)

    A workshop or manufactory (Lewis & Short; see factory): where the maker is a firm, name its works, ex quā officīnā?, which manufacturer?

  • fabricātor, fabricātōris m. — the maker (of a particular thing)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.120: fabricātor minūtōrum opusculōrum (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 2.264

    Rare (Lewis & Short), always with the genitive of what was made; in Vergil the maker of the wooden horse.

  • domus fabricātōria — a manufacturing firm

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. manufacturer, after Egger, with a query on domus

    Morgan–Owens doubts the phrase himself.

See also production, industry, goods, company, producer.

SourcesLewis & Short: opifex · Lewis & Short: officina · Lewis & Short: fabricator

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. manufacturer.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
